run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: Fetched runbook skill_id signup-service-debugging-runbook and carried out its steps with my own tools. Its steps: (1) check signup pod status/logs — carried out via kubernetes_jq_query (pods, app-162) and fetch_pod_logs; both signup pods are Running with restartCount 0 but ready=false, and their logs repeat "Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>" and "GET /ready 503". (2) verify payments service health — carried out; pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-9h6t5 is Running with restartCount 0, ready=false, and its log states "STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail" with "Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key", /ready and /health both 503. (3) test service-to-service communication — could NOT run kubectl exec/curl/port-forward (no exec tool available); substituted Endpoints inspection, which shows the payments-service Endpoints object contains only notReadyAddresses (10.244.0.55) and no ready address, consistent with the connection-refused error. (4) check Stripe / database messages in payments logs — carried out; Stripe messages found, no database error lines appear in the sampled log window. (5) verify env vars — partially carried out; the Deployment shows STRIPE_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL sourced by secretKeyRef from Secret payments-secrets, but secret values cannot be read, so the key value itself could not be verified. Assessment: the signup failures trace to the payments dependency, whose readiness probe fails because the container's STRIPE_API_KEY (from Secret app-162/payments-secrets, key stripe-api-key) is an invalid test key; because payments has no ready endpoint, signup's call to http://payments-service:8080 is refused, signup's own /ready returns 503, and signup therefore has no ready endpoint either. Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable in this Run, so metric/trace corroboration is missing; the finding rests on pod logs, pod/endpoint/deployment state and events.

claims.text: The payments-service container logs at startup: "STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail" (pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-9h6t5, namespace app-162).

The same payments-service log records readiness and liveness failures: "GET /ready" 503 at 17:05:02, 17:05:07 and 17:05:12, "GET /health" 503 at 17:05:06 with "ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key".
Both signup-service pods log repeated "ERROR - Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>" followed by "GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503, from 17:05:02 to 17:05:12.

Deployment payments-service (namespace app-162) injects STRIPE_API_KEY from secretKeyRef name=payments-secrets key=stripe-api-key and DATABASE_URL from key database-url of the same Secret; its readinessProbe is httpGet /ready:8080 every 5s and livenessProbe httpGet /health:8080 every 10s.

The Endpoints object payments-service in app-162 has one subset containing only notReadyAddresses (pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-9h6t5, ip 10.244.0.55, port 8080) and no ready address, so the ClusterIP has no ready backend. The signup-service Endpoints object likewise has only notReadyAddresses for both signup pods (10.244.0.53, 10.244.0.54).

Deployment signup-service sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080, and Service payments-service in app-162 is ClusterIP with selector app=payments-service, port 8080 targetPort 8080, while the payments container port is 8080 — host, port and selector all match.

Pod state in app-162 at query time: payments-service-6d94c44fdc-9h6t5, signup-service-7c89545dc9-jpjp5 and signup-service-7c89545dc9-wf4x9 are all phase Running, container ready=false, restartCount 0, state running, no previous terminated container; all three were created 2026-11-23T17:04:55Z by their ReplicaSets.

Deployment status in app-162 shows both workloads unavailable: payments-service unavailableReplicas=1 and signup-service unavailableReplicas=2, each with condition Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable; both Deployments are at generation 1 (managedFields: kubectl-client-side-apply and kube-controller-manager status write at 2026-11-23T17:04:55Z), i.e. a fresh first rollout, not a template-preserving restart.

Events inside the authorized window across all namespaces group to: Deployment app-162 ScalingReplicaSet (2), Pod app-162 Created/Pulled/Scheduled/Started (3 each), ReplicaSet app-162 SuccessfulCreate (3). No Evicted, OOMKilled, BackOff, Failed or Unhealthy events appear in that grouped view (5 further events fell outside the window and were dropped before grouping).

Namespace app-162 contained no NetworkPolicy objects and no ResourceQuota objects at query time, so neither object class is configured to block signup→payments traffic or cap resources in this namespace.

Secret app-162/payments-secrets (keys stripe-api-key, database-url) is the object from which the payments-service container reads the STRIPE_API_KEY that its own log reports as an invalid test key and that makes /ready and /health return 503.

Rejected: a signup→payments misconfiguration (wrong PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL, wrong Service port/targetPort or wrong selector) causing the connection refused. The URL is http://payments-service:8080, the Service port and targetPort are both 8080 with selector app=payments-service, the container listens on 8080, and the Endpoints object resolves the pod as a notReadyAddress — the refusal comes from having no ready backend, not from a wrong address or port.
Rejected: NetworkPolicy blocking or a ResourceQuota shortage in app-162. Neither kind had any object in the namespace at query time.

Rejected: payments-service crashloop, OOMKill or eviction. The pod is Running with restartCount 0, no previous container instance exists, and no OOMKilled/Evicted/BackOff/Failed events appear in the window's grouped event view.

Rejected: the otel-demo 'payment' Deployment (image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-payment, namespace otel-demo) is the dependency signup calls. signup's PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL points at payments-service in namespace app-162, a different entity from the otel-demo 'payment' workload.

Because signup's readiness depends on the payments check, the signup-service failure (and therefore users being unable to register through a ready signup endpoint) is a consequence of the payments-service readiness failure rather than an independent signup defect; no signup-side error other than the payments check appears in the sampled signup logs.

Correct the stripe-api-key entry in Secret app-162/payments-secrets to a valid key (value must be written by an operator; secrets are unreadable to this investigation), then confirm payments-service /ready returns 200 and the payments-service Endpoints object gains a ready address; signup's /ready should then stop returning 503.

gaps: Secret values cannot be read: the actual value of app-162/payments-secrets key stripe-api-key was not verified; the conclusion that it is an invalid test key rests on the payments container's own log line.

The value of signup's DATABASE_URL (from Secret signup-secrets key database-url) was not verified, and signup's readiness probe exercises only the payments check, so a latent signup database problem cannot be excluded from the sampled readiness logs.

Prometheus was unavailable for every query attempted in this Run (get_label_values, execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so error-rate, request-latency and rpc/payment metric series are unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unavailable (traces_list_services and traces_search returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), so no trace-level call-chain evidence exists for the signup→payments call.
5 events fell outside the authorized window and were dropped before grouping; earlier event history is unknown.
Change history is not integrated, so when Secret payments-secrets was written and with which value cannot be determined; only the current state is observable.

The sampled log windows end at 17:05:12–17:05:22Z (pods created 17:04:55Z), so the failure state is established for that interval only, and no prior healthy baseline for these deployments exists (generation 1, first rollout).
next_steps: Runbook skill_id signup-service-debugging-runbook steps to apply manually: kubectl describe/logs on signup and payments pods in app-162 (done via API here; exec/curl and port-forward could not be run because no exec tool is available) and verify payments /health and /ready after fixing the key.

Replace or rotate the invalid Stripe key in Secret app-162/payments-secrets (key stripe-api-key), e.g. kubectl -n app-162 patch/create the secret, then watch payments-service /ready and the payments-service Endpoints ready addresses.
After payments becomes ready, re-check signup-service /ready and its logs for any remaining payments-check errors, and verify signup-service Endpoints gains ready addresses.
Verify signup's DATABASE_URL/signup-secrets validity separately, since the readiness probe does not exercise the database.
Add monitoring of payments readiness (and of the payments Endpoints ready-address count) so a bad Stripe key surfaces before signup becomes unusable.
